MAJOR: `apply()` flips object-store targets to `exists` because `ref in tables` matched an unrelated Postgres table named `artifacts`; `ref in tables or (kind=="object-store" and ref in tables)` is the same expression twice, so object-store "existence" is proven by a coincidental table-name collision.
`check()` validates only `kind=="table"` targets against migrations; object-store `exists`/`migrated` claims are never verified, so the gate certifies unverified migration state.

Derived `migration_status` silently overwrites deliberate `retained` classifications for file-backed stores to `migrated` and ignores `backend` entirely; no invariant ties `backend` to `target.kind`/status.

`RELATIONSHIPS` is a second source of truth duplicated between the script constant and `store-registry.json`; `--apply` regenerates and silently discards any relationship added directly to the registry.
New blocking gate ships with no automated negative test in the diff despite the acceptance criteria requiring negative-test evidence (exit 1).

SQL is parsed with regex (`CREATE TABLE ... \((.*?)\);`): nested `CHECK(...)`/`numeric(...)` bodies, `PARTITION OF`, and comments can truncate or miss tables, producing false FAILs or silently empty column sets.
MINOR: A `planned` target under a completed owner can fail `check()` while `apply()` cannot flip it (ref not in `tables`), leaving the gate permanently red with only a manual edit as escape hatch.
`REQUIRED_TRIGGERS` hardcodes four audit trigger names; any migration refactor/rename breaks the gate with no provenance to the discovering item.
`_trigger_names()` is re-globbed and re-reads all `*.up.sql` once per required trigger (4x per run) instead of being cached alongside `_tables()`.
All relationships carry `owner_item: BI-PF-1309` rather than the owning EDP item (EDP-15/18/19/20/21), weakening slice/domain traceability required by Slice C.
Failure output truncates to 20 problems without a flag or full-report path, complicating triage in CI logs.
NIT: `verified` in the JSON is a stored assertion redundant with checks the gate already performs; recomputed on `--apply`, so it can only ever be `true` in a passing registry.
`--registry <path>` still resolves migrations/backlog items from `ROOT`, making the alternate-registry option only half-parameterized.
Counts (`migrated/retained/pending`) are computed even on the failure path but only printed on success.
SUMMARY: Solid structural direction: a fail-closed relationship/migration gate wired into both precheck fast and ci-cd-gates, with registry data kept consistent by `--apply`.

Top risks: object-store "exists"/"migrated" evidence is derived from a coincidental table-name match and never independently verified; regex SQL parsing and a duplicated canonical relationship list threaten long-term integrity and maintainability.

Recommend hardening before relying on the gate as compliance evidence: real object-store verification, single source of truth for relationships, backend↔target coherence rule, and committed negative tests.
